Customer to run two-week perf pilot on Dedicated pool (Priya to send config)
Sasha to review SOC2/ISO docs and confirm encryption/KMS questions by 2026-02-25
action_items: Priya Nair: send Dedicated pool config + batching recommendations (due: 2026-02-20)
Dana Cole: confirm pilot success criteria and traffic slices (due: 2026-02-23)

meeting_header: Date: 2026-02-18 | Start: 15:00 PT | Duration: 54m | Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood), Priya Nair (Redwood), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM); Dana, Miguel, Sasha, Ravi (Larkspur)
summary: Quarterly check-in focused on runway (budget/forecast), capacity planning for an upcoming product launch, reliability targets, and a short pilot to validate Dedicated capacity. Customer has strict encryption/KMS requirements and prefers a private deployment if Dedicated results are acceptable. Action items: pilot kickoff, docs handoff, and cost scenarios to inform procurement timeline.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick readout of agenda — runway and capacity, reliability numbers, then pilot planning.
[00:18] Dana: thanks Alex. we are tight on budget this q but launch timeline hasn't moved, so need a plan that keeps latency under 250ms p95 and cost within our forecast.
[00:32] Miguel: yeah, our traffic profile is spiky — afternoons and end of month reports — so autoscale behavior is key. we noticed token costs jumped last month when we increased context windows.
[00:47] Priya (SE): ok that's helpful. on the cost side we usually look at batching + quantization tradeoffs. for a mixed workload with few long-context requests we recommend prefix KV caching and sequence-length aware batching. that tends to shave per-token by roughly 20-35% depending on distribution.
[01:05] Sasha (Security): couple quick items — we need to ensure any Dedicated or Private deployment can integrate with our KMS (HashiCorp Vault) and that audit logs are shipped to our SIEM. is that covered?
[01:18] Samir (CSM): absolutely we'll share the SOC2 and ISO artifacts, plus integration notes for KMS. Priya, can you outline the encryption points during the run?
[01:30] Priya (SE): sure. if you go Dedicated hosted by Redwood, we support customer-managed keys for model payload encryption at rest and in transit via TLS. for Private we can do a direct KMS integration in your VPC, HSM is supported for on-prem. audit logs — we stream to S3 or a syslog sink you control.
[01:49] Dana: great. timeline-wise procurement will need a cost scenario by next week to decide between Dedicated reserved and a Private proof-of-concept.
[02:01] Alex: ok we'll prioritize the cost scenarios. Samir will also pull historical usage and build a 90-day forecast.
[02:10] Miguel: on reliability, we saw a 3x error spike during last week's deploy. it looks like fallback routing didn't kick in cleanly to the cheaper model variant — maybe a config mismatch.
[02:23] Priya (SE): that sounds like a rollout policy edge-case. we had a known bug where canary fallback didn't remap model variants if versions were pinned; I thought that was patched last month though.
[02:33] Dana: hmm maybe. the error happened on a canary rollout. log attached in the ticket we opened (link in the chat).
[02:41] Priya: i'll pull the ticket after this. likely a mapping in the route policy — we'll validate logs and share a short RCA.
[02:48] Alex: sounds good. moving on to pilot scope — customer asked for a two-week Dedicated pilot with a small reserved pool plus autoscale. Priya, what config would you recommend?
[03:00] Priya: for the pilot — start with a 4-GPU pool (A100 or comparable) with autoscale up to 8 for burst, here are the key knobs: continuous batching enabled, kv cache enabled for repeated session flows, a conservative max tokens cap per request, and request priority rules to protect critical routes. we'll provide a JSON config but, uh, sometimes the exported names in the console look different — sorry for the inconsistencies in naming.
[03:30] Miguel: 4 GPUs — do we have predicted latency numbers? p95 250ms is our target.
[03:36] Priya: depends on model. for the Llama-variant you're testing, with batching and kv cache we expect p95 ~180-220ms at nominal load; under 2x burst it could go to 300ms without aggressive batching. we can tighten with quantized weights but need to validate quality.
[03:53] Dana: quality is non-negotiable for the clinical notes feature. any quantization approach that drops accuracy is a dealbreaker.
[04:01] Priya: understood — we'll do a regen test against your eval set. if 8-bit quantization shows >0.5% drop on key metrics we won't recommend it for that route.
[04:12] Sasha: on data residency — some patient data must remain in region. does Redwood let us pin model inference to a region?
[04:19] Alex: yes. you can route to region-specific nodes; for Private we'd run inside your VPC in region. Dedicated pools can be region-pinned too.
[04:28] Ravi: curious about cost math — what's the delta between Reserved Dedicated (monthly commit) vs Private? rough order.
[04:36] Samir: typical delta: Dedicated reserved is lower ops overhead and faster to start — pricing usually includes platform. Private has higher upfront integration and a platform fee but gives full control (and sometimes lower unit price at very large scale). we'll model both scenarios in the spreadsheet.
[04:50] Alex: ok we'll attach a 12-week and 52-week scenario so procurement has runway numbers.
[04:55] [05:00] Dana: quick question — SLA expectations for Dedicated? we need 99.9 for core inference.
[05:06] Alex: our Dedicated SLA targets 99.9 uptime for the reserved pools, and we provide credits for breaches. we'll share the exact SLA doc. for Private we can agree on custom SLAs in contract.
[05:17] Miguel: about the error spike — can we add synthetic monitoring for the pilot so we catch regressions?
[05:23] Priya: yes, Redwood Console can emit latency and token-level traces; we also recommend adding canary traffic split with golden prompts so you can watch quality drift.
[05:34] Sasha: I'm still worried about audit trails. will the console show model input hashes but not full PII? we need to avoid storing raw patient texts in vendor logs.
[05:43] Samir: we have a redaction option — you can opt to store only hashes and metadata, and retain full payloads only in your VPC for Private. we'll include the retention policy in the docs.
[05:57] [06:00] Dana: perfect. moving to pilot success criteria: we'll run the pilot for 2 weeks. success = p95 latency <=250ms for critical route, error rate <0.1%, and no >0.5% degradation on clinical accuracy evals. if those are met procurement will greenlight a 6-month reserved commit.
[06:24] Alex: clear. Priya, you'll own config and support during pilot; Samir will track usage/billing.
[06:31] Priya: yes — i'll send the config and a short runbook with common troubleshooting steps. also will include batching settings and how to interpret KV miss rates — sometimes people think misses are errors but they are expected on first sessions.
[06:46] Miguel: weirdly our engineers saw 400 errors that look like memory pressure on the runtime, stack trace pointed to a cuda allocation fail. could that be due to model variant selection?
[06:58] Priya: cuda alloc issues usually occur when model footprint is larger than GPU memory, or when very high concurrency hits a node. we have mitigations: model sharding, quantization, or routing to larger GPU types. i'll correlate the timestamps with infra logs.
[07:11] Dana: any chance this is our side — we have parallel clients that open many long-lived streams.
[07:18] Miguel: yeah we do keep websockets open for session continuity. perhaps we should cap concurrent streams per session.
[07:25] Priya: that's a good mitigation — set sensible keepalive and cap concurrency. we can simulate your exact pattern during the pilot.
[07:33] [07:45] Alex: procurement asks for a renewal cadence and what metrics we report monthly. Samir, what do you recommend?
[07:51] Samir: monthly report: tokens consumed, cost by route, p95 latency, error rate, and a small quality sample with eval regressions flagged. we'll automate export to your BI.
[08:03] Dana: ok that helps. also, what's the lead time to move from Dedicated pilot to Private on-prem? we may prefer Private later for compliance.
[08:12] Alex: typical path is start Dedicated pilot (2 weeks), then 4-8 weeks for Private PoC integration depending on network and KMS work. we'll lay out a timeline that lines up with your procurement windows.
[08:24] Sasha: who will be our technical point of contact during the Private onboarding?
[08:29] Priya: I'll be the SE lead, with support from the Private deployments team — I'll introduce them in the kickoff invite.
[08:36] [08:50] Miguel: on autoscaling policies — can we set soft and hard caps and a pre-warm cold start buffer for predicted events?
[08:57] Priya: yes — autoscale policies support a pre-warm step and scheduled scaling. we also have a feature to buffer expected traffic spikes (predictive burst) tied to traffic signals.
[09:08] Dana: can Redwood provide a brief A/B of quantization impact on our eval set? we want concrete numbers.
[09:14] Priya: yes. we'll run your eval set on full-precision and 8-bit (and mixed 16/8) and share a delta table. if quality drop > threshold we won't recommend it for core clinical routes.
[09:27] Alex: ok action recap: Priya sends configs + eval run, Samir builds cost/runway scenarios, Dana confirms success criteria, Sasha does compliance review.
[09:38] [09:45] Dana: any other blockers? procurement wants edge-case pricing for spikes and overage caps.
[09:52] Samir: we'll include an overage protection plan in scenarios and show a smoothing curve for budget.
[10:00] Miguel: timeline on docs and configs?
[10:04] Priya: i'll send the pilot config and runbook by 2026-02-19 EOD. Samir will send the cost scenarios by 2026-02-20. Sasha expected SOC2 pack by 2026-02-20 too.
[10:18] Sasha: i'll look for docs and flag any KMS gaps.
[10:22] Alex: perfect. last thing — demo checkpoint mid-pilot?
[10:27] Dana: yes let's do a mid-pilot 30-minute sync after week one to triage.
[10:33] Samir: i'll schedule that.
[10:36] [11:00] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and kickoff invite.
[11:05] Dana: thanks team.
[11:10] End of meeting.
